comment: No source is published; the maker's manual page was not used. The five bank names are Kick&Clap, Snare, Toms, Hat&crash and Extras. The sample number is five times the bank plus the sample knob plus the truncated sample CV, clamped to 0 and 24. THE DECAY KNOB RUNS BACKWARDS FROM WHAT ITS NAME SUGGESTS AND ITS DEFAULT IS THE SHORTEST SETTING. The module computes 1.1 minus the knob, plus a tenth of the decay CV, leaves the sample untouched when that figure is 0.12 or less, and otherwise applies a straight fade of one minus six times the figure times the fraction of the sample played. With the knob at its default of 0 the figure is 1.1, so the fade reaches silence at about 0.15 of the sample; the fade is skipped only above about 0.98 of the knob's travel. The LoFi knob is configured as a continuous 0 to 1 parameter but is only ever compared against 0.5, so it behaves as a two-position switch: above halfway the nearest stored sample is read, below halfway it interpolates between neighbours. Playback speed is the cube of the Tune knob, which is configured 0 to 2 with a default of 1, plus a fifth of the pitch CV, floored at 0.05; the samples are stored at 44100 and the step is scaled by 44100 over the engine rate. The accent and reverse inputs are levels read once, on the frame the trigger starts, not edges of their own. One light is configured, held at 5 while a trigger is high. There is no context menu. Panel lettering came from res/lowFiDrum.svg rendered with rsvg-convert: BANK, SAMPLE, Tune, Accent, LoFi, Trig, Choke, Rev and Out, with the decay knob marked only by a curve and the trigger button unlabelled. The maker's tooltips use different words again: FREQ for the knob the panel prints Tune, ACC for Accent, DECAY for the unmarked knob, and the input names carry the misspelling 'trigerring'.
